items.takeaway: Measure end-to-end time separately from token output rate when selecting a reasoning setting.
items.observation: Artificial Analysis reported around 21 minutes per task for Neon xhigh and 36 minutes for Carbon high.
items.body_notes: The publisher reports that Neon used about 15% more output tokens at a higher output rate. At those different settings it ranked Neon at 61 and Carbon at 60.

items.takeaway: Cache public CelesTrak orbital data and calculate positions in the browser for a navigable 3D view.
items.observation: The video shows satellites and orbital tracks changing as the author moves around the globe.
items.body_notes: The author used Neon to build the tracker and describes how it uses public orbital data to predict positions for objects including Starlink satellites, the ISS, and GPS satellites.

items.title: Train a custom wake word for home automation
items.takeaway: Use Neon in Antigravity to train a custom wake model, then connect the trigger to a separate intent classifier.
items.observation: The demonstration shows the wake-word model running alongside voice-triggered home automation.
items.body_notes: The author shows the trained hey_vanya.onnx model. A separate Gemini Decisions classifier chooses actions, and the author shows Home Assistant deployed by Neon.

items.title: Prototype a video matting workflow in Antigravity
items.takeaway: Use Neon to connect a segmentation tool and a video-matting tool, then compare intermediate frames.
items.observation: The screenshot shows the author's frame previews from a work in progress.
items.body_notes: The author used Gemini 4 Neon in Antigravity alongside Meta SAM 3 and MatAnyone 2. The source shows a prototype and provides no quantitative evaluation.

items.title: Compare four models on a 3D ring animation
items.takeaway: Render the same mechanical ring concept in four versions and inspect them at matching points in the motion.
items.observation: The source places four labeled 3D interpretations side by side as their rings open.
items.body_notes: The video labels the outputs GLM-5.4 Max, Gemini 4 Neon Extra, Claude Fable 5.2 High, and Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh. The author's ranking applies to this demonstration.

items.title: Animate a faux-3D character with stacked sprites
items.takeaway: Build the illusion of depth with stacked sprites and add motion to test it from different angles.
items.observation: The video shows a pixel-art shark rotating above a platform, while the attached still shows a plush-shark reference.
items.body_notes: The author used Neon for a sprite-stacking experiment followed by animation.

items.title: Recreate a Mexico City street in Blender
items.takeaway: Use an agent swarm to build a city scene, then inspect it from street level.
items.observation: The clip shows a daylight street scene with vehicles, storefronts and signs.
items.body_notes: The author reports using the /swarm command with Gemini 4 Neon to recreate Mexico City in Blender.

items.title: Compare two models animating a leaf through seasons
items.takeaway: Give both models the same falling-leaf brief and compare motion, transitions and the reported run cost.
items.observation: The video pairs Gemini 4 Neon xhigh with Astra 6.2 Max on the seasonal scene.
items.body_notes: The author reports 1 h 31 min and $15.36 for Neon, and 46 min 32 s and $10.15 for Astra in this comparison.

items.title: Build an origami carousel that folds on scroll
items.takeaway: Tie the folding animation to scroll position so readers can move through a series of 3D shapes.
items.observation: The demo shows flat sheets folding into shapes such as a boat, butterfly and whale as the carousel moves.
items.body_notes: The author credits Neon with eight sculptures and describes using XPBD folding physics and custom WebGPU shaders.

items.title: Compare Neon token use in paired coding tasks
items.takeaway: Run two models on the same prompt and environment, then compare output tokens, time and tool calls separately.
items.observation: In the author's Agent Duel data, the chart shows median output of about 22,000 tokens for Neon and 11,400 for its matched opponents.
items.body_notes: The OpenCode comparisons also show about 6.1 versus 4.1 minutes and 32 versus 30 tool calls at the plotted medians.

items.title: Compare overnight training experiments on identical GPUs
items.takeaway: Run the same autoresearch task on matching hardware and retest the best changes on held-out data.
items.observation: The author reports 0.994 bits per byte for the original baseline, 0.973 for Opus 5.5, and 0.957 for Neon on held-out text.
items.body_notes: The overnight H100 comparison used Gemini 4 Neon High and Claude Opus 5.5 Medium. Each best result was retrained from scratch for the held-out check.

items.title: Prototype a local inference engine for RTX 5090
items.takeaway: Use an inference optimization skill to tailor an engine to hardware and inspect memory use during a local run.
items.observation: The dashboard shows Inkling 2 Mini running with 22.7 of 32 GiB of GPU memory in use and zero spill.
items.body_notes: The author credits Neon with writing the Zig and CUDA engine. The demonstration shows the resulting engine configured for a context of 1,048,576 tokens.

items.title: Use code-drawn keyframes to guide character animation
items.takeaway: Sketch timing and silhouettes with code-drawn keyframes before handing the sequence to a video model.
items.observation: The video shows several character examples and their keyframe timelines.
items.body_notes: The author credits Neon with drawing five keyframes in code and H3 Max with turning those drawings into the final animation.

items.title: Build a dungeon explorer with manual takeover
items.takeaway: Pair automatic exploration with a control the player can take over in an isometric game.
items.observation: The Three.js prototype shows a character exploring torchlit rooms and finding loot.
items.body_notes: The author credits Neon with the game and says the player can take control at any point.

items.title: Build a map for tides and drain reports
items.takeaway: Combine public weather and tide information with locally reported clogged drains in a map.
items.observation: The demonstration shows San Francisco map layers and individual drain report panels.
